result.noFurtherDiscriminator: All 6 turns observed. The core was successfully picked up (turn 2), so the affordance was realized. The failure is that hostile fire (Raider Holt's scatter-blast repeatedly hitting Medic Reyes) and reactor environmental damage (10/turn to Imani and Chen) killed the medic and prevented extraction. No unobserved turn remains to further discriminate between survival-pressure vs. local-policy-choice; the evidence clearly shows the team was executing the intended aggressive recovery but was blocked by survival pressure before extraction could complete.
result.rationale: The trajectory shows the team successfully reached the Research Core (Engineer Imani picked it up at turn 2) and the affordance was locally available and legible. The core was acquired. However, the team was then progressively ground down by sustained hostile pressure and environmental reactor damage. Medic Reyes took repeated scatter-blast hits (25 dmg at turns 2, 3, 4, 5) dropping from 90 to 0 and died at turn 5. Engineer Imani and Security Chen each took 10 environmental reactor damage every turn they remained in the reactor zone (turns 2-5), and reactor heat climbed to 100. The core was picked up but the team could not extract it because survival pressure (hostile Raider Holt's repeated attacks on the medic, plus reactor environmental damage) blocked the team before the core could be carried out. The intended probe was to accept higher tactical exposure to recover the core — the team did accept exposure and did recover the core, but the survival/spatial pressure (hostile fire + reactor hazard) killed the medic and prevented extraction. This is a survival-spatial-pressure bottleneck: the affordance (core pickup) was realized, but health/position/hostile pressure blocked the useful action (extracting with the core) from becoming actionable.
